critiques.weakest_assumption: The team can correctly classify and seed hundreds of heterogeneous claims while also building an empty backend and demonstrating a product.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: By deadline the team ships migrations, joins, and a partial basil fixture rather than complete eight-crop data, APIs, and usable screens.
critiques.hidden_cost: The real workload is curator time assigning roles, bases, scopes, and provenance to 674 absences plus narrative claims, then debugging rejected inserts.
critiques.best_fix: Cut the interval child, composite basis constraints, and full-corpus extraction; use a 64-row coverage table plus a tiny one-to-many typed claim table for the 3–5 usable ranges and important warnings.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Calling SQLite a rebuildable cache assumes a reliable semantic rebuild process even though two documents resist deterministic extraction.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: The cache becomes manually maintained JSON with inconsistent payload shapes, fragile eligibility queries, and application branches for every exception.
critiques.hidden_cost: Curators must atomize claims, preserve Korean caveats, invent payload conventions, and keep generated columns synchronized with those conventions.
critiques.best_fix: Drop generic payloads and automated extraction; version a validated manifest containing 64 explicit coverage records and a small typed claims list, using enums rather than JSON-string matching.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Mandatory human approval can process enough LLM-generated records to justify a compiler, hashes, manifests, stable IDs, and registry migration during a hackathon.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: The team demonstrates an impressive pipeline over 20 records while most crops remain unreviewed and the actual product has little seeded content.
critiques.hidden_cost: Korean domain review, candidate adjudication, stable-ID policy, source-span maintenance, reproducibility tests, and eight-crop registry reconciliation dominate engineering time.
critiques.best_fix: Cut LLM extraction, hash gates, line locators, and the general compiler; manually curate only the coverage matrix and usable claims with document-section provenance.

critiques.weakest_assumption: One crop-axis row can represent both coverage and multiple semantically different claims without pushing complexity into an opaque blob.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: Basil’s optimum, injury threshold, and disease conditions are overwritten, conflated, or decoded through frontend-specific JSON logic.
critiques.hidden_cost: Someone still must reconcile 674 absence markers into 64 judgments, adapt section-9 guidance, and manually detect drift after document changes.
critiques.best_fix: Keep the minimal JSON loader but split it into a 64-row coverage table and a small one-to-many claims table keyed by claim kind, with simple source-section columns instead of an audit blob.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Deployments will supply precise scope and trustworthy calibration metadata sufficient to make context-dependent eligibility more useful than a fixed reviewed disposition.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: Exact matching yields almost no scores, after which deadline pressure produces hardcoded calibration exceptions that falsely look evidence-backed.
critiques.hidden_cost: The team must seed deployment scopes, model use cases, govern calibrations, obtain reference measurements, and test a combinatorial matching engine.
critiques.best_fix: Cut local conversion and calibration escape hatches; store a reviewed SCORABLE, ADVISORY_ONLY, or RECORD_ONLY disposition per crop-axis-use-case and limit scoring to the validated temperature cases.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Every unscored cell has section-9 guidance that can be safely condensed, scoped, translated, and reviewed before the deadline.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: The dashboard ships dozens of generic advisory cards and misleading disease-risk numbers surrounding only three defensible gauges.
critiques.hidden_cost: The uncounted work is curating 64 coverage judgments, rewriting Korean guidance, designing three frontend states, and implementing provenance drill-down.
critiques.best_fix: Honor the crossed threshold by cutting the gauge-first layout, advisory numeric bands, and rich drill-down; ship crop guidance pages with telemetry charts, explicit coverage reasons, and only three solid temperature bands.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Historical replay and SQLite write contention are immediate product risks worth solving before the empty backend can ingest and display telemetry.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: Two connections, revision semantics, and replay code consume the hackathon while delivering no visible value and still fail across schema migrations.
critiques.hidden_cost: Dual-file migrations, coordinated backups, revision-aware queries, seed snapshots, retention rules, and timestamp correctness all require design and testing.
critiques.best_fix: Use one WAL-mode SQLite database and record a corpus commit or knowledge-release ID on seeded records, keeping the corresponding seed JSON in git and deferring replay.

critiques.weakest_assumption: Stakeholders will accept a condition monitor with almost no scoring as a successful interpretation of the intended product.
critiques.likely_failure_mode: Without careful scope, the demo becomes generic sensor charts, zero-axis crops appear useless, and instantaneous temperature alerts flap.
critiques.hidden_cost: The team still must build telemetry ingestion, charts, crop selection, honest empty states, and vetted qualitative content despite removing scoring.
critiques.best_fix: Cut push alerts and all invented thresholds; ship charts, clearly labelled guidance, and range-membership indicators only for the three instantaneous-compatible temperature ranges, using operational debounce solely for display stability.

decision_crux: Can stakeholders accept a guidance-first condition monitor with only three defensible temperature bands; if yes, combine H with a repaired D and slim F, while if no, none of the richer schemas can manufacture a buildable evidence-backed score product.
